correctness.rationale: For arbitrary \(n\ge3\) and \(z\), normalizing the single-site vector by \(D=n-1+|z|^2\) is strictly legitimate. The Weyl projector-Gram eigenvalue identity \(n|B(a,b)|^2/D^2\) was reconstructed and checked against arXiv:2106.01509v1 Theorem 2. The complete four-case correlation computation yields mutually disjoint zeros on two coordinate axes and among \(a,b\) both nonzero. Fixed-a congruence solution counts grouped by \(\gcd(a,n)\) prove the totient sum \(C_n(r)\), including composite moduli and \(b=0\) subtraction for \(r=0\). The center \(z=1\) has exactly \(n\) projector directions. The prime test follows from \(C_n(0)=\sum_{a=1}^{n-1}(\\gcd(a,n)-1)\), and \(z=2+2i\) works because its phase ratio has nonintegral rational trace \(6/5\) and thus is not a root of unity. The bundled CHECK.py was executed from its actual package path and agreed with 48 direct complex projector-span ranks plus 52 exact modular counts. These finite checks are not the infinite proof; the displayed derivation supplies that proof.

value.rationale: The constant Weyl fiducial has rank n, so a one-coordinate deformation is a natural minimal-symmetry-breaking family for tomography. Rather than merely observing generic full rank, the theorem supplies an exact algebraic parameter discriminant and number of irrecoverable operator directions, including composite zero-divisor multiplicities and overlaps. It exposes an exact primality test within a natural one-real-parameter slice and an explicit fixed rational-complex fiducial complete in every dimension, useful for deterministic tomography. These are a complete motivated classification, not a finite ad hoc enumeration or a relabelled known inequality; stability and SIC optimality are expressly not claimed.
